purpose: Test whether an 8-bit fixed-schema UDP application header reduces Stage-9.7 framing overhead while preserving the same causal and fail-closed protocol behavior.

data_policy.input: registered protocol fixture and synthetic UDP fault schedule only

compact_header.length_inference: frame kind plus UDP datagram payload byte count

comparison_rules: H32 and H8 overhead are computed on the identical realized frame ledger.
Each normal-path H8 datagram must save exactly 24 bits relative to H32.
Protocol actions, fault schedule, endpoint state machines, ports, and proxy behavior are unchanged.
Timing is descriptive and excluded from selection and reproducibility hashes.

batching_analysis_only.scope: ideal upper bound for fixed 42-bit ordinary updates
batching_analysis_only.adoption_status: not eligible without task-regret evaluation on temporal spectrum traces

claim_boundary: The 4-bit magic is only a framing discriminator; inner protocol magic and version checks remain mandatory.
The compact header is not an authentication or integrity code.
The result applies only to the registered fixed schema and allowed update lengths.
Batching results are analytical upper bounds, not adopted protocol results.
No IPv4, UDP, link-layer, retransmission, or cryptographic overhead is claimed as measured.
A positive transport result does not reverse the Stage-6 external Final failure.
